subject: Climate & Environment
title: Food Waste and Climate Change
description: Learn Food Waste and Climate Change in one minute.

hook.text: Growing food that nobody eats wastes the water, land, energy, and fuel used to produce it.

buildup.text: Food waste accounts for roughly 8 to 10% of all global greenhouse gas emissions.

discovery.text: When food rots in landfills, it produces methane — far more warming than CO₂ per molecule.

twist.text: Reducing food waste is one of the most effective climate actions any person or business can take.

climax.text: Project Drawdown ranks food waste reduction as the number one climate solution available.

punchline.text: Eating what you buy is a climate action. A simple, delicious one.

quiz.question: What share of global greenhouse gas emissions comes from food waste?

details.summary: Food waste accounts for roughly 8 to 10 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions when including production, transport, and decomposition in landfills.
details.whyItMatters: Cutting food waste requires no new technology and delivers immediate climate, economic, and humanitarian benefits. It is one of the most accessible climate solutions for individuals and businesses.
takeaways: Food waste produces 8 to 10 percent of global emissions
Project Drawdown ranks food waste reduction as a top solution
Reducing waste also saves water, land, and economic resources

faq.question: What is the link between food waste and methane?
faq.answer: When food decomposes in oxygen-deprived landfill conditions, it produces methane rather than CO2. Methane is over 80 times more potent as a greenhouse gas over 20 years. Diverting food to composting or anaerobic digestion captures or avoids this methane.

faq.question: What can individuals do to reduce food waste?
faq.answer: Plan meals and shop with a list, store food properly to extend freshness, understand date labels, use leftovers creatively, compost scraps that cannot be eaten, and buy imperfect produce. Household changes alone could significantly reduce total food waste.
